name: BASIC Web
tagline: A from-scratch BASIC compiler and runtime for building interactive web pages.
problem: Nostalgia theme: modern web development is buried under frameworks; what if you could build for the web with 1960s-simple imperative code?
solution: A TypeScript parser, compiler and runtime that turns BASIC programs into HTML, with the project's own website written in BASIC and shipped via CI to GitHub Pages as a single bundled file.
demo_moment: Open a to-do app and reveal it was written entirely in BASIC.

why_it_stood_out.claim: Most of the team had no compiler experience and built parser, IR and runtime in 36 hours — visible, verifiable depth.
Theme answered through a programming language rather than a retro UI skin.
Shipped, not mocked: deployed site, CI/CD and dependency scanning.
Won two prizes (overall 2nd and a sponsor prize), showing one project can stack a main-rubric win with a sponsor lane.

lessons: A no-AI project with genuine depth can out-place AI wrappers; depth is most persuasive when the demo proves it (the site itself is BASIC).
